{"parentUuid":null,"isSidechain":true,"promptId":"bd7356ac-a34b-468e-9a5f-4f41165c71f1","agentId":"ab17500a6f17ce8c1","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"Review target: `86`\n\n`minimal prompt → single careful diff pass → ≤15 findings`\n\nYou are reviewing a pull request for real bugs. Treat this diff as the review scope.\n\nReview the diff as a careful senior engineer would: read every hunk, open the surrounding files for context as needed (Read, Grep, git log/blame/show), and hunt for correctness issues — wrong or inverted conditions, off-by-one, null/undefined dereference, missing `await`, dropped error handling, removed guards or validations, broken callers of changed functions, races. {"parentUuid":"ad3ed6aa-3c64-4952-bebc-50159562713f","isSidechain":true,"agentId":"ab17500a6f17ce8c1","attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.\n- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: \"chart\", \"graph\", \"plot\", \"data viz\", \"visualization\", \"dashboard\", \"analytics\", \"visualize data\", \"categorical colors\", \"sequential / diverging palette\", \"stat tile\", \"sparkline\", \"heatmap\", \"legend\", \"axis\", \"tooltip\", \"chart colors\", \"color by series\".\n- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.\n- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.\n- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.\n- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.\n- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.\nTRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it \"looks like a one-liner\" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).\nSKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).\n- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). {"parentUuid":"3f6ae957-2e3b-4e5e-a77e-f44f3785c122","isSidechain":true,"agentId":"ab17500a6f17ce8c1","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CevwZZinS1hU4PWKHbkvD","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_0184H43VTVwmekQStDBXtur7","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"git status --short && git log --oneline -3","description":"Check working tree"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":19185,"cache_read_input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":222,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":19185},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":222,"cache_read_input_tokens":0,"cache_creation_input_tokens":19185,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":19185,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"requestId":"req_011CevwZZ1sFmmyzwxb8HS19","attributionSkill":"code-review","type":"assistant","uuid":"0776b314-e516-4e35-9bb7-b71b66ecf053","timestamp":"2026-09-11T03:28:00.067Z","effort":"high","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/workspace","sessionId":"d07c2d64-4203-482c-a30e-3c51db52e69a","version":"2.1.235","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"3f6ae957-2e3b-4e5e-a77e-f44f3785c122","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"bd7356ac-a34b-468e-9a5f-4f41165c71f1","agentId":"ab17500a6f17ce8c1","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_017hqpP3vKnL8bcNtVvDUwVP","type":"tool_result","content":"{\"baseRefName\":\"main\",\"body\":\"Closes #82.\\n\\n`services.charge()` is `@transaction.atomic`, so `apply_to_class()` opened a\\nsavepoint per entry: a 45-child three-line bill opened **135 subtransactions**\\ninside its one transaction, against the **64** subtransaction ids PostgreSQL\\ncaches per backend. Past 64 the backend overflows and every *other* backend's\\nvisibility check against those xids falls back to `pg_subtrans`, for as long as\\nthe transaction stays open.\\n\\nThis is **option 1** of the three the issue set out: an inner `_charge()` with\\nno savepoint, called only by `apply_to_class()`, while the public `charge()`\\nkeeps its decorator.\\n\\n## Why option 1 and not the other two\\n\\n**Option 2 (`bulk_create()`) buys speed by dropping `full_clean()`**, which\\nstops `Model.clean()`'s cross-row rules and the FK probes being asked and breaks\\nthe \\\"every entry funnels through `_post()`\\\" invariant — the same funnel #83's\\nfinding 1 was about. Weakening that in the money path is the wrong trade.\\n\\n**Option 3 gives up all-or-nothing billing**; a partially billed class is worse\\nfor a bursar than a slow one.\\n\\nTwo functions rather than one with the decorator removed, because `charge()`'s\\nown docstring has warned since the schedule work that *\\\"the second caller is the\\none that will not know\\\"*. That caller must find the safe function under the\\nobvious name.\\n\\n**The savepoint bought the charge loop nothing**, and that is structural rather\\nthan a judgement: the loop catches nothing, so an `IntegrityError` rolled back\\nto its savepoint and then propagated out of `apply_to_class()`'s own atomic\\nblock, aborting everything the savepoint was protecting.\\n\\n## Measured before the fix was written\\n\\nA 45-child three-line class. Statements counted with `CaptureQueriesContext`;\\nthe transaction held open while a second connection scanned 20,000 times.\\n\\n| children | rows | subtransactions | statements | wall |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| 10 | 30 | 30 | 318 | 0.096s |\\n| 45 | 135 | **135** | 1,368 | 0.363s |\\n\\nPer entry: 1 SAVEPOINT + 1 RELEASE + 1 INSERT + 2 SELECT + 5 SET = **10 statements**.\\n\\n| case | subxids | reader µs/scan | `Subtrans` blks_hit | blks_read |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| 45 children, via the service | 135 | **39.45** | **8,100,003** | **0** |\\n| 45 children, one insert | 0 | 12.29 | 1 | **0** |\\n| 10 children, via the service | 30 | 7.31 | 3 | **0** |\\n| 10 children, one insert | 0 | 7.52 | 4 | **0** |\\n\\nThe one-insert rows are the control: **the same number of tuples to check, zero\\nsubtransactions**, so the row count is held fixed and the subxid effect is\\nisolated. `8,100,003` = 20,000 scans × 135 tuples × 3 lookups per tuple.\\n\\n**It is a step, not a slope.** At 30 subtransactions the service and its control\\nare identical within noise and the counter does not move; at 135 it is 3.2× and\\n8.1 million lookups. The threshold is 64 ÷ 3 lines = **22 children**, so every\\nordinary class was past it. A 45-child class is the median Nigerian secondary\\nclass.\\n\\n### Cache lookups, not disk\\n\\n**`blks_read` is 0 in every row above, including the 8.1-million one.** All of it\\nwas served from the in-memory Subtrans SLRU cache; there is no disk I/O anywhere\\nin these numbers. PostgreSQL 15's Subtrans cache is a fixed 32 buffers\\n(~65,536 xids) and nothing here comes near exhausting it. Worth stating because\\nit bounds the damage honestly: bad enough to triple every concurrent reader, not\\nbad enough to cause I/O storms.\\n\\n### The caveat that matters, for whoever benchmarks this next\\n\\n> **The cost is zero on an idle cluster.** My first run showed all zeros, and\\n> the reason is real: `XidInMVCCSnapshot()` returns \\\"in progress\\\" immediately\\n> for any xid ≥ the snapshot's `xmax`, so while nothing else commits, the\\n> billing subxids sit above every reader's `xmax` and `pg_subtrans` is never\\n> consulted. I had to run a committer alongside (8k–21k commits) to advance\\n> `latestCompletedXid` before the effect appeared. In production that committer\\n> is other schools' ordinary traffic — so this is **off when the cluster is\\n> quiet and fully on when it is busy**, which is the honest form of #82's \\\"paid\\n> cluster-wide\\\" claim.\\n\\nA benchmark run against a quiet database will show this fix changing nothing,\\nand conclude it was unnecessary. It is not: it is measuring the one condition\\nunder which the bug does not appear.\\n\\n## The control run\\n\\n`SubtransactionCountTests` counts savepoints rather than timing anything,\\nbecause the count is the mechanism and a timing here would be a flake.\\n\\nReverting the one word — `services._charge` back to `services.charge` — with the\\ntests in place:\\n\\n```\\nRan 4 tests in 8.386s\\nFAILED (failures=3)\\n\\nFAIL: test_billing_a_class_opens_one_savepoint_not_one_per_charge\\nAssertionError: 5 != 1 : one savepoint for apply_to_class()'s own atomic block\\nand no more; a savepoint per charge is issue #82\\n\\nFAIL: test_the_count_does_not_grow_with_the_class\\nAssertionError: 7 != 1 : the savepoint count must be flat in the size of the\\nclass; that is the whole of #82, since 64 is the limit and a class is not\\n\\nFAIL: test_a_discount_still_opens_one_because_its_handler_needs_one\\nAssertionError: 7 != 3 : one for the run and one per concession; if this ever\\nreads 1 the collision handler has lost the savepoint it rolls back to\\n```\\n\\n**`5` and `7` are the subxid count growing with the class** — two children then\\nthree, one savepoint per charge on top of the run's own. After the fix all three\\nread the run's savepoint plus one per concession and nothing more:\\n\\n```\\nRan 4 tests in 8.565s\\nOK\\nEXIT=0\\n```\\n\\n`test_charge_still_leaves_an_enclosing_transaction_usable` **stayed GREEN\\nthroughout**, and correctly: the control does not touch `charge()`, and that\\ntest asserts the guarantee the decorator still buys. That is the control's own\\ncontrol — had it moved, the control would have been proving something else.\\n\\n## Deliberately not fixed here\\n\\n**The discount loop still opens one savepoint per concession, and must** — its\\ncollision handler needs one to roll back to, and removing it reintroduces the\\nbug where one collision leaves forty-five children unbilled. That leaves this\\nfunction under 64 **by margin rather than by construction**, since a class\\ncannot have more concessions than children. Filed as **#85** with the numbers in\\nit, to be measured rather than guessed at.\\n\\n**The 683 `SET search_path` statements** of the 1,368 — five per entry, from\\ndjango_tenants — are untouched, and are a separate and larger question about the\\ntenant backend. Note that #82's own estimate of ~675 statements was **half** the\\nreal figure; that is where the other half went.\\n\\n## Runs\\n\\n| target | result |\\n|---|---|\\n| `fees` | `Ran 106 tests in 182.126s`, `OK`, `EXIT=0` |\\n| `results.tests.test_withholding` | `Ran 69 tests in 281.169s`, `OK`, `EXIT=0` |\\n| `makemigrations --check` | `No changes detected` |\\n\\n`test_withholding` because it is the neighbour: it charges children into arrears\\nthrough `fees.services.charge()`, which is the function this PR splits.\\n\",\"headRefName\":\"charge-subtransactions\",\"state\":\"OPEN\",\"title\":\"A class of forty-five bills in one subtransaction, not a hundred and thirty-five\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/adedejimakinde/luffy-school-saas/pull/86\"}","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"d9e641df-1281-4f9c-ab3f-adc897bb11ce","timestamp":"2026-09-11T03:28:01.283Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"3f6ae957-2e3b-4e5e-a77e-f44f3785c122","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/workspace","sessionId":"d07c2d64-4203-482c-a30e-3c51db52e69a","version":"2.1.235","gitBranch":"main"}

The only supported way to write one.\n\nFour functions, one per thing that can happen to a family's account: they are\ncharged, they pay, they are given a discount, or somebody made a mistake and it\nis undone. There is deliberately no general \"adjust\" — see `reverse_entry()`.\n\nEverything here takes the caller's *student membership id* rather than a\n`Membership` object, because the ledger stores a bare id and the two must not\ndrift apart. `snapshot_student()` is the one place that turns a live membership\ninto the frozen identity an entry carries.\n\nNo screens, no HTTP. This is the data layer the eventual bursar's screen will\ncall, and keeping the rules here rather than in a view is what makes them true\nfor an import and a management command too.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom django.db import transaction\nfrom django.utils import timezone\n\nfrom accounts.students import why_not_a_student_here\n\nfrom .models import FeeEntryKind, FeeLedgerEntry, LedgerIsAppendOnly\n\n\nclass FeeLedgerError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"A ledger entry could not be posted as asked.\n\n    One base class for the whole module, for the same reason\n    `schools.models.InvitationError` is one for the invitation flow: a caller\n    that writes `except FeeLedgerError` should catch every refusal this module\n    makes, not the half it happened to import.\n    \"\"\"\n\n\nclass NotPositive(FeeLedgerError):\n    \"\"\"An amount was zero or negative where a magnitude was wanted.\n\n    Every function here takes the amount as a plain positive number of kobo and\n    applies the sign itself. Letting a caller pass a negative to `charge()`\n    would make the sign a caller's choice, and the sign is the ledger's whole\n    grammar.\n    \"\"\"\n\n\nclass AlreadyReversed(FeeLedgerError):\n    \"\"\"That entry has been undone once already.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass CannotReverse(FeeLedgerError):\n    \"\"\"That entry is not one that can be undone.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass NotThisTermsLine(FeeLedgerError):\n    \"\"\"The schedule line named belongs to a different term than the charge.\n\n    `a_schedule_line_charges_a_child_once` is keyed on\n    `(student_membership_id, source_line)` and carries no term, on the argument\n    that a line belongs to a schedule which belongs to exactly one term, so the\n    pair is already term-scoped. That is true of the *line* and false of the\n    *caller*: nothing stopped a hand-typed charge naming this term and last\n    term's line. The index then reads that entry as this line's charge for the\n    child, and the next `apply_to_class()` run reports their tuition as\n    **skipped** and never bills it -- silent under-billing, discovered when a\n    parent asks why their invoice is short.\n\n    No constraint can express this: the rule spans `FeeLedgerEntry`,\n    `FeeScheduleLine` and `FeeSchedule`, so it has to be asked in code.\n    \"\"\"\n\n\nclass NotThisStudentsConcession(FeeLedgerError):\n    \"\"\"The concession named belongs to a different child than the discount.\n\n    The mirror of `NotThisTermsLine` on the other new column, and the one that\n    corrupts a *question* rather than a balance:\n    `a_concession_discounts_a_child_once_per_term` is keyed per student, so\n    Chidi's bursary posted against Ada's account is accepted by the index, and\n    \"everything this concession did\" then answers with two children -- while\n    Chidi's own discount still posts later, because that pair is untaken.\n\n    `_require_student_of_this_school()` already guards the child half of every\n    entry this carefully. This is the same guard for the source half.\n    \"\"\"\n\n\nclass NotThisSchoolsStudent(FeeLedgerError):\n    \"\"\"The membership named is not a student of the school whose books these are.\n\n    This is the check that earns the bare id. `student_membership_id` has no\n    foreign key — see docs/tenancy.md for why — which means the database will\n    happily store *any* integer there, including the id of a child at another\n    school entirely. Nothing about that would be visible: the entry would sit in\n    St Mary's ledger, count towards a St Mary's balance, and name a student St\n    Mary's has never taught.\n\n    A foreign key would not have caught it either, note. `Membership` is shared,\n    so a foreign key into it constrains only that the row *exists* — every\n    school's students are in the same table. The school half of the question has\n    to be asked in code whichever way the column is declared.\n    \"\"\"\n\n\ndef _require_student_of_this_school(membership):\n    \"\"\"Refuse a membership that is not a student here, before anything is written.\n\n    The rule itself now lives in `accounts.students` — see the note on\n    `NotThisSchoolsStudent` above, which said it would move there once a third\n    tenant app asked the same question. What stays here is the *raising*, so\n    that `except FeeLedgerError` still means \"the entry was not posted\".\n    \"\"\"\n    reason = why_not_a_student_here(\n        membership, subject=\"a fee entry\", holder=\"books\"\n    )\n    if reason:\n        raise NotThisSchoolsStudent(reason)\n    return membership\n\n\ndef snapshot_student(membership):\n    \"\"\"The identity fields an entry freezes, taken from a live membership.\n\n    Kept in one place because getting it wrong is silent: an entry posted with\n    a blank name is unreadable a year later, and one posted by joining to the\n    live row rewrites itself when a school corrects a spelling.\n    \"\"\"\n    return {\n        \"student_membership_id\": membership.pk,\n        \"student_name\": membership.name,\n        \"student_reference\": membership.reference,\n    }\n\n\ndef _post(*, membership, term, kind, amount_kobo, narration, effective_on,\n          reference=\"\", recorded_by=None, reverses=None, source_line=None,\n          source_concession=None):\n    \"\"\"Create one entry. Every public function below funnels through here.\"\"\"\n    _require_student_of_this_school(membership)\n    entry = FeeLedgerEntry(\n        term=term,\n        kind=kind,\n        amount_kobo=amount_kobo,\n        narration=narration,\n        reference=reference,\n        effective_on=effective_on or timezone.localdate(),\n        recorded_by_id=getattr(recorded_by, \"pk\", recorded_by),\n        reverses=reverses,\n        source_line=source_line,\n        source_concession=source_concession,\n        **snapshot_student(membership),\n    )\n    # `full_clean()` rather than a bare save: the cross-row rules for a reversal\n    # live in `Model.clean()` because no check constraint can express \"equal and\n    # opposite to another row\". Excluding nothing, so the field-level rules are\n    # asked here too rather than only at the database.\n    entry.full_clean(exclude=None, validate_unique=False, validate_constraints=False)\n    entry.save()\n    return entry\n\n\ndef _magnitude(amount_kobo):\n    if not isinstance(amount_kobo, int) or isinstance(amount_kobo, bool):\n        raise NotPositive(\n            f\"Amounts are whole kobo as an int, not {type(amount_kobo).__name__}. \"\n            f\"A float cannot hold a naira amount exactly, which is the reason \"\n            f\"this column is kobo in the first place.\"\n        )\n    if amount_kobo <= 0:\n        raise NotPositive(\n            f\"Pass the amount as a positive number of kobo; the ledger applies \"\n            f\"the sign. Got {amount_kobo}.\"\n        )\n    return amount_kobo\n\n\ndef _charge(membership, term, amount_kobo, *, narration, effective_on=None,\n            reference=\"\", recorded_by=None, source_line=None):\n    \"\"\"`charge()` without the savepoint. **`fees.schedules` only.**\n\n    Issue #82. `charge()` is `@transaction.atomic`, so every call inside\n    `apply_to_class()`'s one transaction opened and released a savepoint, and a","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"731c229d-2054-4d15-b4f1-10fe953e5b92","timestamp":"2026-09-11T03:28:24.931Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b99949ec-62af-44a8-8f59-3349d2e355cd","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/workspace","sessionId":"d07c2d64-4203-482c-a30e-3c51db52e69a","version":"2.1.235","gitBranch":"main"}

Increases what the family owes.\n\n    `source_line` is passed by `fees.schedules` and left null by every hand-typed\n    charge. It is what makes \"everything this line of the bill did\" a question\n    with an answer, and what the idempotency index keys on.\n\n    **A caller passing `source_line` must hold the schedule's row lock**, the way\n    `schedules.apply_to_class()` does. `a_schedule_line_charges_a_child_once`\n    refuses a second charge for one child and line, and outside that lock two\n    writers can both pass a skip-check and one will meet the index. Today this\n    module has exactly one such caller, so the race is not reachable; the note is\n    here because the second caller is the one that will not know.\n\n    Raises `NotThisTermsLine` if the line belongs to another term's bill.\n\n    The savepoint this decorator opens is the whole difference between this and\n    `_charge()`: it is what lets a caller inside a larger transaction catch a\n    refusal and carry on. `apply_to_class()` is the one caller that provably\n    does not need it, and issue #82 is what that savepoint cost. The term check\n    below is asked here rather than left to a constraint, because no constraint\n    can reach across three tables to ask it -- and it is free in the hot path,\n    since `apply_to_class()` reads its lines through `locked.lines.all()` and a\n    reverse manager primes each line's `schedule` from the instance it came\n    from, so this compares two integers already in memory.\n    \"\"\"\n    return _charge(\n        membership,\n        term,\n        amount_kobo,\n        narration=narration,\n        effective_on=effective_on,\n        reference=reference,\n        recorded_by=recorded_by,\n        source_line=source_line,\n    )\n\n\n@transaction.atomic\ndef record_payment(membership, term, amount_kobo, *, narration=\"Payment received\",\n                   effective_on=None, reference=\"\", recorded_by=None):\n    \"\"\"Record money received. Reduces what the family owes.\"\"\"\n    return _post(\n        membership=membership,\n        term=term,\n        kind=FeeEntryKind.PAYMENT,\n        amount_kobo=-_magnitude(amount_kobo),\n        narration=narration,\n        effective_on=effective_on,\n        reference=reference,\n        recorded_by=recorded_by,\n    )\n\n\n@transaction.atomic\ndef discount(membership, term, amount_kobo, *, narration, effective_on=None,\n             recorded_by=None, source_concession=None):\n    \"\"\"Reduce what is owed without money changing hands.\n\n    A bursary, a staff child's concession, a sibling discount. Its own kind\n    rather than a negative charge, because \"we waived it\" and \"they paid it\" are\n    different facts and a school's books have to be able to tell them apart.\n\n    Raises `NotThisStudentsConcession` if the concession is another child's.\n    \"\"\"\n    if (\n        source_concession is not None\n        and source_concession.student_membership_id != membership.pk\n    ):\n        raise NotThisStudentsConcession(\n            f\"Concession {source_concession.pk} belongs to membership \"","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"ab1d8c21-c7eb-4cb2-98ae-e2c630f77d56","timestamp":"2026-09-11T03:28:26.697Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"c678f713-ff23-419c-89bd-d290ae0810f5","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/workspace","sessionId":"d07c2d64-4203-482c-a30e-3c51db52e69a","version":"2.1.235","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"a9c89a34-47b6-456c-bc8b-3ea3c8cca068","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"bd7356ac-a34b-468e-9a5f-4f41165c71f1","agentId":"ab17500a6f17ce8c1","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MM7322PJk42Q9XqR212ES2","type":"tool_result","content":"    }\n    missing = [sid for sid in student_ids if sid not in memberships]\n    if missing:\n        raise UnknownStudent(\n            f\"{class_group} has placements naming memberships that no longer \"\n            f\"exist: {missing}. The roster has to name real students before the \"\n            f\"class can be billed.\"\n        )\n\n    # **A child whose membership has ended is not billed**, and this is the same\n    # call `academics.services` already made. `place_student()` deliberately\n    # allows an ended child to be placed — entering last term's roster after the\n    # fact is real work and those children have often left — and its docstring\n    # says why the automated path must not follow: it is the one \"that would\n    # repeat such a mistake silently across a whole school\".\n    # `carry_forward_placements()` filters them out and calls that \"a correctness\n    # rule and not a tidiness one\". Applying a bill is the same kind of path:\n    # nothing deletes a `ClassPlacement` when a membership ends, so a child\n    # released in December is still on JSS 1A's roster in January, and a bursar\n    # adding one line to that term's bill and re-running would charge them.\n    #\n    # Skipped rather than refused, because refusing is the forty-five-children\n    # outcome again: one child having left must not stop the class being billed.\n    # Counted, though — `students_skipped` — because a skip nobody is told about\n    # is the silent no-op this module refuses everywhere else.\n    # Decided from the read above, whose `status` is loaded -- see that comment\n    # for why the loading, and not the join, is what makes this correct.\n    billable_ids = [sid for sid in student_ids if memberships[sid].is_live]\n    students_skipped = len(student_ids) - len(billable_ids)\n    student_ids = billable_ids\n\n    # Both skip-sets in one query each, and both are read *after* the lock, so a\n    # concurrent application of this bill has either not started or has finished.\n    # `order_by()` with no arguments on both: these collapse into a `set()`, and\n    # `FeeLedgerEntry.Meta.ordering` would otherwise have Postgres sort every\n    # matching row by `-effective_on, -id` for an answer that discards the order.\n    already_charged = set(\n        FeeLedgerEntry.objects.filter(\n            kind=FeeEntryKind.CHARGE,\n            source_line__in=lines,\n            student_membership_id__in=student_ids,\n        )\n        .order_by()\n        .values_list(\"student_membership_id\", \"source_line_id\")\n    )\n\n    # **`order_by()` explicitly, because this one carries a concurrency\n    # guarantee.** Two runs of two *different* schedules in one term can both\n    # reach the same `(child, term, concession)` row — that is the collision the\n    # foot of this function handles. If they reach *several* such rows in\n    # different orders, Postgres does not hand back a unique violation; it hands\n    # back a deadlock, SQLSTATE `40P01`, which arrives as `OperationalError` and\n    # not as `IntegrityError`. The handler below cannot see it, so the loser's\n    # whole transaction dies and the class goes unbilled — the outcome the skip\n    # exists to prevent, reached by the one route the skip cannot cover.\n    #\n    # A total order shared by every run is what makes the cycle impossible. That\n    # order is `FeeConcession.Meta.ordering` and this queryset inherited it\n    # silently, so the guarantee held by accident and one `Meta` edit would have\n    # removed it with nothing going red. Named here, and pinned by\n    # `test_the_concession_read_is_ordered_so_two_bills_cannot_deadlock`.\n    concessions = list(\n        FeeConcession.objects.filter(\n            is_active=True, student_membership_id__in=student_ids\n        ).order_by(\"student_membership_id\", \"id\")\n    )\n    already_discounted = set(\n        FeeLedgerEntry.objects.filter(\n            kind=FeeEntryKind.DISCOUNT,\n            term=term,\n            source_concession__in=concessions,\n            student_membership_id__in=student_ids,\n        )\n        .order_by()\n        .values_list(\"student_membership_id\", \"source_concession_id\")\n    )\n\n    charges_posted = charges_skipped = charged_kobo = 0\n    discounts_posted = discounts_skipped = discounted_kobo = 0\n\n    # **`services._charge()`, not `services.charge()`, and the underscore is the\n    # whole of issue #82.** `charge()` is `@transaction.atomic`, so calling it\n    # here opened a savepoint per entry and a 45-child three-line bill opened\n    # 135 subtransactions inside this one transaction. Postgres caches 64 per\n    # backend; past that it overflows and every *other* backend's visibility\n    # check against those xids falls back to `pg_subtrans`, for as long as this\n    # transaction stays open. A test that only ever exercises the skip\nwould pass identically against a schema with no index at all, which is exactly\nthe shape of green test `docs/operating-rules.md` rule 5 is about.\n\n**Two schools throughout.** A fee schedule is per schema, and every \"this\nschool's bill\" claim below is asserted against a second school that must be\nuntouched — a single-tenant test cannot tell a correctly scoped query from one\nthat quietly bills the wrong children.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom django.db import IntegrityError, connection, transaction\nfrom django.db.models import ProtectedError\nfrom django.test.utils import CaptureQueriesContext\nfrom django.test import TestCase\n\nfrom academics import services as academics\nfrom academics.models import ClassGroup, Term, TermName\nfrom accounts.models import Membership, MembershipStatus, User\nfrom accounts.services import enroll_student\nfrom fees import schedules, services\nfrom fees.models import (\n    FeeConcession,\n    FeeEntryKind,\n    FeeLedgerEntry,\n    FeeSchedule,\n    FeeScheduleLine,\n    KOBO_PER_NAIRA,\n)\nfrom schools.tests.tenants import connected_to, make_school\n\nPASSWORD = \"correct-horse-battery\"\n\nTUITION = 120_000 * KOBO_PER_NAIRA\nLEVY = 15_000 * KOBO_PER_NAIRA\n\n\nclass BillingSetUp(TestCase):\n    \"\"\"Two schools, each with a JSS 1A, a first term, and children in it.\n\n    St Mary's is the school under test. {"parentUuid":"9847d89a-5bb9-4ffc-af91-9ac914148dfe","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"bd7356ac-a34b-468e-9a5f-4f41165c71f1","agentId":"ab17500a6f17ce8c1","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01JWk3nUA8Z37QAJpM6SAvWx","type":"tool_result","content":"    def _other_terms_line(self):\n        \"\"\"A line on a second term's bill for the same class.\"\"\"\n        with connected_to(self.stmarys):\n            other_term = Term.objects.create(\n                session=\"2025/2026\",\n                name=TermName.SECOND,\n                starts_on=date(2026, 1, 12),\n                ends_on=date(2026, 4, 3),\n            )\n            other_bill = FeeSchedule.objects.create(\n                term=other_term,\n                class_group=ClassGroup.objects.get(pk=self.group_id),\n            )\n            return FeeScheduleLine.objects.create(\n                schedule=other_bill, description=\"Tuition\", amount_kobo=TUITION\n            )\n\n    def test_a_charge_naming_another_terms_line_is_refused(self):\n        \"\"\"Silent under-billing, and the index would have accepted it.\n\n        `a_schedule_line_charges_a_child_once` is keyed on `(student, line)` with\n        no term. A hand-typed correction naming this term and last term's line\n        therefore *fills that child's slot*, and the run that should bill them\n        reports a skip instead. Nothing raises, nothing is missing from the\n        ledger to look at, and the child is simply never charged tuition.\n        \"\"\"\n        line = self._other_terms_line()\n\n        with connected_to(self.stmarys):\n            with self.assertRaises(services.NotThisTermsLine):\n                services.charge(\n                    self.ada,\n                    self.term(),\n                    TUITION,\n                    narration=\"Tuition correction\",\n                    source_line=line,\n                )\n\n            # Nothing posted, so the slot is still free -- which is the half\n            # that matters. A refusal that still consumed the slot would be the\n            # same bug wearing an exception.\n            self.assertEqual(self.balance_of(self.ada), 0)\n            summary = self.apply()\n            self.assertEqual(summary.charges_posted, 4, \"the class billed normally\")\n            self.assertEqual(summary.charges_skipped, 0)\n            self.assertEqual(self.balance_of(self.ada), TUITION + LEVY)\n\n    def test_the_refusal_is_a_fee_ledger_error(self):\n        \"\"\"`except FeeLedgerError` has to keep meaning \"nothing was posted\".\"\"\"\n        self.assertTrue(\n            issubclass(services.NotThisTermsLine, services.FeeLedgerError)\n        )\n        self.assertTrue(\n            issubclass(services.NotThisStudentsConcession, services.FeeLedgerError)\n        )\n\n    def test_a_discount_naming_another_childs_concession_is_refused(self):\n        \"\"\"The index is per student, so this posts and corrupts the question.\n\n        `a_concession_discounts_a_child_once_per_term` is keyed\n        `(student, term, concession)`. Chidi's bursary posted against Ada takes\n        the `(Ada, term, bursary)` pair, which nothing else wanted -- so it is\n        accepted, Chidi's own discount still posts later, and \"everything this\n        concession did\" answers with two children and twice the money.\n        \"\"\"\n        with connected_to(self.stmarys):\n            chidis = FeeConcession.objects.create(\n                student_membership_id=self.chidi.pk,\n                amount_kobo=TUITION,\n                reason=\"Staff child\",\n                granted_by_id=self.bursar.pk,\n            )\n\n            with self.assertRaises(services.NotThisStudentsConcession):\n                services.discount(\n                    self.ada,\n                    self.term(),\n                    TUITION,\n                    narration=\"Staff child\",\n                    source_concession=chidis,","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"eab06bcb-8c72-49f0-a556-e1f31fcb0991","timestamp":"2026-09-11T03:29:29.287Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"9847d89a-5bb9-4ffc-af91-9ac914148dfe","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/workspace","sessionId":"d07c2d64-4203-482c-a30e-3c51db52e69a","version":"2.1.235","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"aefb1a28-e74f-4d5d-a507-d9ad41d9d240","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"bd7356ac-a34b-468e-9a5f-4f41165c71f1","agentId":"ab17500a6f17ce8c1","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01RaTu8tutukhEQdw6g77EXY","type":"tool_result","content":"            self.assertTrue(reversal.narration.startswith(\"Reversal of: Tuition, \"))\n            self.assertTrue(\n                reversal.narration.endswith(\"\\u2026\"),\n                \"the cut is marked, so the tail is not read as the whole thing\",\n            )\n            self.assertEqual(reversal.amount_kobo, -charge.amount_kobo)\n\n    def test_the_reversal_lock_does_not_join_the_term(self):\n        \"\"\"`FOR UPDATE` on a joined term row is what stalls a billing run.\n\n        Every entry `apply_to_class()` inserts takes `FOR KEY SHARE` on the\n        term row for its foreign-key check and holds it to commit, and that\n        conflicts with `FOR UPDATE`. One bursar clicking undo on an unrelated\n        payment would wait out a forty-five-child billing run; in the other\n        order the billing run stalls on its first insert. Asserted against the\n        compiled SQL, because the join is invisible in the Python.\n        \"\"\"\n        with connected_to(self.stmarys):\n            self.apply()\n            charge = FeeLedgerEntry.objects.filter(\n                kind=FeeEntryKind.CHARGE\n            ).first()\n\n            with CaptureQueriesContext(connection) as captured:\n                services.reverse_entry(charge, recorded_by=self.bursar)\n\n        locking = [\n            q[\"sql\"] for q in captured.captured_queries if \"FOR UPDATE\" in q[\"sql\"]\n        ]\n        self.assertEqual(len(locking), 1, \"one locking read, on the entry\")\n        self.assertNotIn(\n            \"academics_term\",\n            locking[0],\n            \"the lock joins the term again, so it takes FOR UPDATE on that row\",\n        )\n\n    def test_the_line_guard_costs_no_query_per_charge(self):\n        \"\"\"A guard paid 135 times inside the lock would be its own finding.\n\n        `apply_to_class()` reads its lines through `locked.lines.all()`, and a\n        reverse manager primes each line's `schedule` from the instance it came\n        from -- so the check compares two integers already in memory. Concrete scenario: a 45-child class where each child has a bursary and a sibling discount → 90 savepoints in one transaction, back over the 64-subxid cache, with exactly the cluster-wide `pg_subtrans` cost this PR was written to remove. Even 1.5 concessions per child on a 45-child class (68) crosses it.
